winner.title: Kabsa (Spiced Chicken and Rice)

evidence.authenticity: Recognizable kabsa: bone-in chicken browned then cooked with basmati in a tomato-spice base, loomi (dried lime), cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, ghee, topped with fried almonds, pine nuts and raisins, served with daqoos and yogurt. Carrot, allspice and orange zest are modest home-cook adaptations. Author is not confirmed as Saudi, so not full marks.
evidence.precision: Weights for 11 of 29 ingredients (onion 10 oz/283 g, tomatoes 255 g, carrot 170 g, rice 400 g, water 600 ml); chicken sized as 4 thighs and 4 drumsticks, about 2.5 lb; large Dutch oven; 25 sensory cues in 7 steps (skin golden, tomato mixture jammy and sticking, rice edges translucent, golden crust, nuts lightly golden). No oven temperature needed except for the optional broil.
evidence.testing: Serious Eats test-kitchen style, with salting-time reasoning, notes on ghee vs oil, rice rinsing and loomi substitution. Only 2 ratings, so little public feedback. The page's why-it-works text was not confirmed.
evidence.photos: All 7 steps have images in the schema (7 step images); 66 images on the page in total.
evidence.efficiency: Total 1 hr 5 min. The topping is made while the rice cooks, and the chicken is browned in the same pot. The optional broil and 30-minute salting add a little time.
evidence.access: Loomi lime is the only specialty item, and the recipe gives a lime-peel strip substitute. Daqoos is optional. Everything else is at a normal US grocery.

winner.why: It is the only candidate with step photos, weights, a pan size and a doneness cue on nearly every step, from a test-kitchen publisher.

runnerUp.title: Chicken Kabsa (Arabian Chicken and Rice)

evidence.authenticity: Traditional layout: homemade kabsa spice mix, bone-in chicken, dried limes, rice cooked in tomato-spice broth, oven-browned chicken, fried onion, nut and raisin garnish.
evidence.precision: Only 1 of 33 ingredients has a weight; 4 oven temperatures and 19 sensory cues; Dutch oven size not given.
evidence.testing: No stated reasoning or testing beyond one rating.
evidence.photos: No step images in the schema; process photos not confirmed.
evidence.efficiency: 80 minutes; the first stage is somewhat long, and it yields 12 servings.
evidence.access: Dried limes are used, with a lime powder substitute.

runnerUp.why: A more traditional-style recipe than the quicker versions, but it has less precision and no process photos.

candidates.disqualified: read returned HTTP 403, so it was not scored
